summary: The root كَمَمَ primarily means to cover or conceal something, often by wrapping or enclosing it. It can refer to covering a pot, a sword in its sheath, or a woman's head.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.

headwords.def: كَمْ: see its syn. كَأَىٍّ or كَأَيِّنْ voce أَىٌّ. As an interrogative with the specification suppressed, What number? How many? and, as in an ex. voce سِقْىٌ, virtually meaning How much? and so in an ex. voce مَسَافَةٌ and voce شَبْرٌ. Also How long? as in the Kur, ii. 161, &c.; a noun signifying a period of time being understood: see also an ex. voce عَسَفَ, and voce فَرَشَ.
كَمٌّ and كَمٌ are both app. right: see قَدْ.
كِمٌّ The calyx of a flower. (K, &c.) كِمٌّ The envelope [or spathe ] of the طَلْع [or spadix of a palm-tree ]: and the covering [or calyx ] of flowers or blossoms; as also. (S, Msb, K.)
كُمَّةٌ A قَلَنْسُوَة: (TA in art. بطح:) or a round قلنسوة: (S, K:) pl. كِمَامٌ. (K, * TA in art. بطح.)
كَمِّيَّةٌ Quantum, or quantity, as answering to “ how many. ”
مُكَمَّمٌ Covered over, or concealed ( مَسْتُور ). (S, art. خصب.) See بُرْأَة.
كَمْكَامٌ The cancamum-tree: see بُطْمٌ and ضِرْوٌ.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
